title: The regular affine unit germ generates its ambient stalk freely
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], x in an affine open U, and let H, b and c : O_{X,x} -> H(Gamma(X,U)) be the explicit maps of [def-sc-affine-free-basis-germs]. Then c, sending r to r b, is bijective.

source.place: Tag 01HV, Lemma 26.5.4 (7), natural associated-sheaf stalk localization; Tag 01IB, affine module sheafification; Tag 01C6, finite free sheaves; Tag 0098, restriction along the affine chart; direct-image stalk computed on the cofinal neighbourhoods contained in U

proof.text: Use the explicit regular-module sheaf isomorphism from the basis-germ construction. It takes the sheafified regular module to the unit sheaf on the slice site.

On neighbourhoods V contained in U, the product U times V is isomorphic to V by the second projection. The ordinary direct image of the unit sheaf therefore has the same sections, restrictions and scalar actions as the structure sheaf on those neighbourhoods. Cofinality computes its stalk as O_{X,x}, with the unit germ equal to 1. Multiplication by that germ is bijective. Transport through the explicit regular-module isomorphism gives c.
